body.a world's clock: its tick is a sixteenth of the generation at which the mean walls of the starts it learns from thin to 0.1655, to the nearest 2 generations; its window runs from 16 ticks to 64
excluded_seen: Step 4f (examples/scale-up-class) ran these 29 worlds and the still world on side 1,024 to generation 4,096 from starts 17001 to 17744 and 17901 to 17908, and read them at the still world's tick with nothing of a block's past in view. The worlds and their groups here are chosen from its verdict.

The sizing look (sizing.py here, exploratory, on a rented pod): eleven of these worlds and the still world run again from starts step 4f had used (two or four each, among 17001 to 17664 and 17901 to 17904), read every two generations, and put through this study's own run and every measure of it, both ways round. Every bound here was drawn from it; the bound of J, of worlds it did not see, from what it showed of the others. The worlds it saw are marked in `worlds`: five of the ten that step 4f found served, one of the four nearly served, none of the five just missed, and five of the ten missed. Eighteen were not in it.
Steps 4g to 4i read the still and the busy world with a block's past in view; the look's rule tried here was learned in the still world on side 2,048 from starts 18001 to 18008.
No start from 20001 on has been generated or run on a grid of this size (the study's tests run three of these worlds from theirs on side 128).
body.not_tested: A claim about a world is not tested where its walls give it no tick whose window ends inside a run of 5120 generations, or the larger species has more than 0.8 of the live cells at generation 4,096. A rank correlation is not tested over fewer than 8 worlds. And no claim is tested without a number to judge.

readings.as it is: the leader, and how many of the eight neighbours each species leads
readings.with how long in view: the same, and for how many ticks running the block has had its leader, up to 8

sizing.the worlds between: one of the four nearly served was sized, and none of the five just missed. The claims J of those five rest on no run of them. In the nine sized worlds where step 4f found the still world's rule 0.48% or more from the world's own at its best pace, the look's plain rule on the world's own clock is 1.3 to 2.2 times as far. With how long in view it is 2.3 and 2.4 points nearer in the world nearly served, and 1 to 88 points further in the five missed. Step 4f missed the five between by 3.8% to 6.9%
sizing.two starts or four: the still world, B345/S02457 and B25/S078 have two starts to learn from and two to try on, as the registered run has; the other nine have one and one. Those three read with one and one as well (four ways each) give, on average: the share of surprise that how long removes 0.6 to 1.0 points lower (a rule with more in view has more to learn); the look's rule with how long in view 0.9 to 1.1 points of surprise better beside the world's own in the first two (a world's own rule that has learned from less is the worse rule), and 9 points in B25/S078, where it is 150% worse; the look's plain rule beside the world's own the same to 0.3 points; and every run-on and every ratio of run-ons the same to 0.01, a single trial start lying up to 0.05 from that. So in the registered run the nine should remove nearly a point more than here, and the look's remembering rule should stand a point less well beside the world's own, one tick ahead
sizing.what a claim stands on: in every sized world the larger species has 0.52 to 0.57 of the live cells at generation 4,096 (the bound is 0.8), and every one has a tick, the longest 64 generations (the bound is 80)
sizing.where the runs were made: on a rented pod (2026-11-27; the thirty fine runs side by side and both ways round in 18 minutes), this machine being taken by another job. Twelve of the thirty had been made here first: their leaders and shares are the pod's, entry for entry. And the records of four worlds, made again here from the kept runs with the study's code as registered, are the pod's byte for byte

body.statement: The still world and 29 worlds that keep its clock are each read on their own clock: a tick set by their walls, and a window from 16 of those ticks to 64. Read so, the still world is the still world of steps 4g to 4i (X); every world is the same picture (S) at the pace step 4f read (T); and the look's plain rule, unchanged, keeps every one when run on (K). A block's past matters in the worlds step 4f found served and not in those it missed by a tenth or more (P); one tick ahead the look's rule serves the first and not the second, where remembering makes it worse (O), nor does it serve any of the five worlds step 4f just missed, as it is or with how long in view (J). In the worlds served the look's remembering rule gains on its plain one, runs the world, and does it as the world's own does (D); in the worlds missed it does not gain (W), though there the look's rules run a world on better than the world's own (B). Over all of them, the more the old rule missed a world the less its blocks' past matters and the less remembering gains (G). So the rule that remembers does not reach the worlds the plain rule missed: it carries the worlds the plain rule served, better. Of the four worlds step 4f found nearly served nothing more is claimed; every world is counted against the same bars in the verdict.
